added.long_description:
Mass Magnetics turns recycled rare-earth scrap into high-performance permanent magnets, made in America. The materials we supply are the backbone of electric motors, sensors, speakers, hard drives, and electronics.
Our process enables DFARS-compliant magnets for defense, aerospace, and industrial manufacturers who demand domestic supply without compromising on quality.
Operations in Greater Boston, MA (Greentown Labs) and Columbus, IN.

added.name: Bernard
added.long_description:
Bernard builds AI employees for home and commercial appliance servicers. They work across phone, text, email, warranty feeds, and existing systems to manage customer communication, scheduling, and dispatch, carrying each job through diagnosis, parts preparation, technician handoff, and follow-up. At the center is Pre-ID, which combines the exact appliance and its symptoms with repair history, similar completed visits, manufacturer guidance, and parts data to produce a diagnosis, ranked parts, and follow-up questions. Technicians arrive prepared with the right parts, helping servicers complete more repairs on the first visit.

We’re building the world’s most efficient appliance servicers, creating happier customers and a more connected appliance ecosystem.

Learn more at https://bernardhq.com/
added.one_liner: AI employees that run home appliance repair companies

added.name: Waybill
added.long_description:
Hardware teams burn weeks on procurement. An engineer needs a part. Someone emails five distributors, chases quotes, gets an approval, wires the money, tracks a shipment across three carriers, clears customs, and then nobody knows where the box is or what's actually on the shelf.

Waybill runs that entire loop. Send us a part, a spec, or a BOM. We source it, pull quotes, route approvals, pay the supplier, handle freight and customs, track it to your dock, and keep your stock count updated. 

Take your supply chain for granted.

Built by a team that's seen it at LAT Aerospace and WareIQ (YC S20).
added.one_liner: Managed procurement & inventory for hardware teams.

long_description.before:
Riften is a drop-in replacement for OpenAI and Anthropic APIs. Change one env var. We route each request to the cheapest model that can handle it, including open-weight models we host. Customers cut inference cost before any training begins.

Because Riften sits in the request path, real tasks and their outcomes become training data the company controls. We use that to post-train private models on open weights around recurring work. Those models earn production traffic by matching the APIs they replace.

Over time, frontier APIs handle only the tasks that still require them. The rest runs on models the company owns, on infrastructure it controls.
long_description.after:
Intelligence will be the most valuable asset a company owns. Today, almost every company rents it.

Companies pay a handful of labs one token at a time. Each dollar buys an answer, not an asset. They spend more, but own nothing more.

Riften reverses that.

Change one environment variable and Riften becomes the gateway for a company's AI traffic. We route each request to the lowest-cost model that can do the job, serving most work on open-weight models we host. Customers save money immediately without rebuilding their products.

The gateway is the entry point. Over time, Riften turns the company's work into private models built on open weights and shaped around the business. What begins as cheaper inference becomes an intelligence stack the company owns, runs on infrastructure it controls, and uses to power its most important applications.

We call this earned intelligence. It is created by the company's own work, controlled by the company, and accumulated over time.

The next generation of companies will not rent their intelligence. They will earn it, own it, and compound it. Riften is how they get there.

one_liner.before: Cut LLM spend, then post-train owned models from production traffic.

long_description.before:
Stratum builds AI agents that clear the U.S. government backlog. Every permit, license, patent, drug approval, and benefits claim in America has to be reviewed by a government adjudicator and the software they rely on was built decades before AI. The result is millions of applications stuck in queues: veterans waiting on disability ratings, families waiting on pensions, builders waiting years to break ground.

Stratum replaces that workflow. A reviewer drops in an application, selects the rubric it needs to be checked against, and an agent plans, executes, and reviews the file end to end routing each step to the right model for the most accurate and cost-efficient decision. Hundreds of agents run in parallel in the cloud, with a human kept in the loop to approve and full auditability at every step, so an entire backlog can be cleared in the time it used to take to review a single file.

We're rebuilding the entire infrastructure the government runs on both the reviewer side and the applicant side - so filing and adjudication become instant instead of taking weeks.

We're Vihaan and Raj, brothers. Vihaan was founding engineer #3 at Cadastral (acquired by Legora) and dropped out of Waterloo to build Stratum. Raj led GTM at Deel, averaging 220% of quota over two years and ranking top 5 of 1,000+ reps globally, and dropped out of grad school at the University of Bath to build Stratum.
long_description.after:
Stratum Industries is the applied AI company for governments. We build AI agents that automate the slow, complex manual workflows governments run on, starting with application review, where files are still reviewed by hand, one at a time, leaving millions stuck in queues. 

Stratum's agents review applications end to end with a human in the loop and full auditability, clearing entire backlogs in a fraction of the time. Our mission is to deploy AI across every vertical inside the government, saving agencies tens of billions in administrative cost and making the government one of the most efficient institutions in the world.

one_liner.before: AI agents that clear the U.S. government backlog.

long_description.before:
Denta is the practice management platform that puts dental practices on autopilot. When a dentist starts a new practice, instead of finding an accounting firm, hiring two front desk workers, and then spending their nights posting insurance payments, they use Denta.

I started Denta to help operate my Dad's 10 practices in Iowa. In supporting those, I realized the most painful part was both people and agents having messy access to fragmented data. So I solved for that and now spend my time automating work for dentists!
long_description.after:
Denta saves you money on dental insurance.

When you go to buy dental insurance, instead of picking the plan where 25% of your money goes to Brokers, CEOs, and Administrators, you pick the plan where 100% of your money goes to the dentist.

I started Denta by building software for my dad's 10 dental practices in Iowa. In scaling that product to 13k MRR in 10 weeks, I realized I was working on a small problem in dentistry. Existing software sucks, no doubt, but what dentists complain about even more: insurance.

Insurance is a massive burden on the industry. Dental Software companies make $6B/year. Dental Insurance Companies make $100B/year. 25% of that is wasted on administrators, brokers, and c-suite salaries. As the son of a dentist, I will not let these companies continue to burn $25B/year. That money should go to dentists via reimbursements, patients via more coverage, and employers via reduced costs.

one_liner.before: The dental practice that runs itself
